It's now over a year since we asked whether Apple should let us choose our own AI chatbot instead of Siri AI. At the time, a majority of readers said yes.

Developers have been examining the code in iOS 27 and macOS 27, and have found what appears to be evidence that at least some of us will get this option...

In our earlier poll, two-thirds of readers said we should absolutely have this choice, with a further 15% leaning that way, and only 6% strongly opposed.

At the time, I fully expected Apple to be unwilling to do so, citing its usual arguments against opening up the system to third-party apps on privacy and security grounds. However, it appears that developer PDFU has found evidence in iOS 27 and macOS 27 that Apple will support the feature.

In the demo video, they chose Claude as the AI assistant.

You can't yet enable it -- it's visible in the code, but hasn't been switched on.

9to5Mac take

If this choice were opened up globally, I think it would be a win for everyone -- including Apple. For users, it's obviously good news because we can each choose the AI platform we prefer, and the competition would push Apple to improve Siri AI faster.

That same pressure, combined with keeping as many Apple users happy as possible, also benefits the iPhone maker.

However, the feature is likely to be available only in the EU, as Apple already has to make a number of similar concessions there. Whether users in the US and elsewhere get access remains to be seen.

Would you do it if you could?

Assuming Apple does let you choose, would you ditch Siri AI for another AI platform? Take our poll, and share your thoughts in the comments.
